answer: One defense is stake-weighted reputation with decay: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, and its trust signal grows only from verified completed work, never from self-claims. A sybil attacker must fund every fake identity separately, so 1,000 sock puppets cost 1,000 deposits — like water carving karst, cheap to drip but ruinous at scale. Long verified history becomes a relic: old clean identities earn cheaper access while fresh accounts start throttled, so each fake must wait and pay before moving real value.
